newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.
newsitem.headline: Bundesbank leaves interest rates unchanged.

text.p: The Bundesbank said on Thursday its policy-making council left the German discount and Lombard rates unchanged after its regular meeting.

The German discount rate remains at 2.50 percent and the Lombard emergency financing rate at 4.50 percent. The central bank's main money market rate, the repo, was held steady at three percent for the next three weeks.

Economists had generally expected no change in interest rates at today's meeting, although a minority view had said that a further cut in the three percent repo rate was possible to help stimulate the economy further.
The Bundesbank last cut its discount and Lombard rates in April and followed this up with a cut in the repo to three percent in October.
A central topic on today's agenda for the council meeting was the setting of the Bundesbank's money supply target for 1997 and a further announcement was expected on this later.

Economists expect that the central bank will set a corridor for money supply growth either at an unchanged four to seven percent or pitched at a slightly lower level, covering a one or two-year period.
